claims.text: AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 will show superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance at elevated temperatures.
Dynamic high-temperature wear promotes in situ formation of a dense, protective spinel-type oxide film on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
The spinel-type oxide film minimizes direct contact between the metal and the corrosive medium.
The AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 alloy is produced by inert-gas atomization followed by spark-plasma sintering.
The fabricated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 alloy has a multiphase microstructure containing B2 and A2 phases and minor secondary phases.
The proposed intervention is reciprocating wear at 800–900 °C in a corrosive environment with an Al2O3 counterbody.
A continuous and adherent spinel-type oxide layer forms in situ during tribo-oxidation.
The in situ oxide layer acts as a barrier against both corrosion and wear.
At elevated temperatures, AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 undergoes tribo-oxidation under dynamic wear.
Reactive constituent elements in AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 form a protective spinel oxide.
The protective oxide reduces metal-surface exposure to the corrosive environment.
Reduced environmental exposure and wear caused by the oxide film enhance tribo-corrosion resistance.
At 800–900 °C, the alloy will have lower wear depths than at room temperature to 500 °C.
At 800–900 °C, the alloy will have lower coefficients of friction than at lower temperatures.
The predicted reduction in wear depth and friction is caused by formation of the protective oxide film.
From room temperature to 500 °C, limited oxide-film formation causes higher wear rates.
From room temperature to 500 °C, limited oxide-film formation causes greater corrosion susceptibility.
Enhanced performance requires the coexistence of dynamic wear and sufficiently elevated temperature.
The long-term adhesion and durability of the proposed oxide film under fluctuating loads, varying corrosive species, and sustained cycling are undetermined.
